title: Sage and Sea Salt Focaccia
changes_from_base: Chopped sage in the dough, oil-coated whole sage leaves pressed into the dimples and coarse salt on top.
summary: A classic olive oil focaccia flecked with chopped sage and topped with crisp whole leaves and crunchy sea salt.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast and chopped sage together, pour in the warm water and 2 tbsp oil and mix to a sticky, shaggy dough. Cover for 15 min, then work in the fine salt with wet fingers.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Fold the dough over itself from four sides every 30 min, four times in all, until it is glossy, stretchy and visibly bubbly.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Oil the tin with 2 tbsp oil, settle the dough in and turn it over once. Cover and let it relax and puff for about 1 h, stretching it to the corners after 30 min.

steps.title: Leaves
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230 °C (210 °C fan). Toss the whole sage leaves in a small bowl with the last 1 tbsp oil so they are slick all over; the coating stops them scorching and turns them crisp.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Dimple the dough firmly, press a leaf into each hollow and scatter with the coarse salt.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22-26 min, until the top is golden and the sage leaves are crackly but still green; the centre reads about 96 °C. Rest on a rack 20 min before cutting.

tips: Coat every sage leaf in oil; dry leaves turn brown and bitter in a hot oven.
Press the leaves well into the dimples so they do not lift off as the dough rises.
Coarse salt adds crunch, but go easy if you are watching your salt intake.
storage: Best the same day. Keep wrapped at room temperature for up to 2 days and refresh at 200 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
